label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
D. Bergeron, you are right about one thing: you deserved a straight answer before the 4th, not a mysterious sign. So here it is, with no riddles.

**The bakery is not closing, and we are not moving. I have bought the building.**

I wanted to keep this as a happy surprise for the reopening, but I see now that waiting was a mistake, especially with the rumours going around. M. Ferland, who owned the building, is 81 and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. He offered it to me before offering it to anyone else, and we signed at the notary on December 15.

Marc-Antoine, your cousin is therefore half right: the building was sold. It was sold to me. The ground floor is not becoming a bank, a vape shop or condos. It remains Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré, at 5 Fairmount, on the corner, where we have been since March 2009.

M. Ferland has come in every morning for 17 years for his baguette *pas trop cuite*. He cried a little at the notary. This sale was not easy for him, but he wanted the bakery and the apartments to remain what they are. So did I.

The dates are exactly these: **we will be closed from January 4 to January 18 for the work, and we will reopen on Tuesday, January 19 at 7:00 a.m.**

There are two reasons for the work. First, we are getting a new four-deck oven from our supplier in Laval. Our present oven dates from 1998 and has broken down three times this year. Anyone who has arrived hoping for a particular loaf and found that we could not bake it knows that this has become necessary. Second, we are taking over the space at the back that used to be storage for the dépanneur. There will be six small tables. After all these years of people asking, you will finally be able to sit down with your coffee and your bread instead of balancing everything on the way home.

Now, about the carnets, because this is important and I do not want anyone left wondering.

We sold **214 carnets in October**, each one costing **$60 for 12 loaves**. Every carnet is still valid. There is **no expiry date**, and you do not have to use up your loaves before January 4. The two weeks of work change nothing. If you have seven loaves left, you still have seven loaves left. If you have not used any, all twelve are still yours.

Also, every carnet holder will receive **one free croissant during January**, as a thank-you.

And if somebody still feels uncomfortable and would rather have the carnet refunded, come and see me. I will refund it, with no questions and no hard feelings. I would rather have that conversation face to face than have somebody sitting at home wondering whether their $60 has disappeared.

Noodle_and_crumb, I understand why the timing bothered you, particularly when you saw the sign just after buying one. You do not need to defend yourself for asking. The carnets were not a plan to collect money and disappear, and nobody is going to lose their bread.

The sign itself was written by my nephew Thomas at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking enough about how it would look from the sidewalk. He was excited for me. If the wording caused worry, that is my responsibility, not his. In our heads it meant, “Come back and see the oven and the tables.” I realize that on a door, beside half-empty shelves and a rumour about a real-estate sale, it could mean something much worse.

As for those shelves on the 28th: we had sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches. That is why they looked so empty. It had nothing to do with closing the business.

I also want to speak directly to the tenants upstairs, since they may be hearing these rumours too. **The three apartments stay rented, with the same tenants and the same rent. I have promised them that in writing.** Nobody is being asked to leave because I bought the building. I did not want them to learn something different through gossip on the street.

I understand why people are nervous. Mile End has lost too many small shops, and we have all seen a “temporary closure” turn into something permanent. I am not going to pretend that the word “scam” did not hurt, though. Seventeen years on this street, learning people’s names, knowing who wants which loaf, seeing children grow up—it is painful to think that somebody could believe I would take their money and vanish. But anger is not a very useful answer. The facts are a better answer, and that is why I am giving them here.

Priya, thank you for defending us, and thank you to the others who did the same. Thank you also to everyone who simply asked what was happening instead of deciding the worst. And Bergeron, thank you for asking me directly. You are a regular, and you were right that people deserved more than “big news soon.”

Please consider this the official announcement, a little earlier than planned. We open again **Tuesday, January 19, at 7:00 a.m.**

Then on **Saturday, January 23**, I would like everyone to come by for the reopening celebration. There will be **coffee and a piece of bread from the new oven, free**. Come see the tables, say hello, and let me thank you properly. That invitation includes everyone in this thread—the supporters, the worried people and the sceptics too.

We are staying. And I hope to see you at the counter.
